description: Knowledge Explorer page — a two-tab interface for searching external knowledge sources (DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Sploitus, OSV.dev, Perplexity) and viewing system-wide knowledge acquisition statistics. The Search tab provides three search modes (Web, Error Research, Vulnerability) with result cards showing provider attribution, relevance scores, CVSS badges, and expandable content. The Stats tab displays a metrics dashboard with per-provider counters, cache hit rates, ingestion counts, and a provider availability grid.

groups.name: Page Layout and Structure
groups.description: The Knowledge Explorer page occupies the full tab content area with a top tab bar (Search | Stats) and a scrollable content region below. The layout uses flex-col with h-full to fill available space.

assertions.description: The page fills the entire available height of the tab content area without leaving empty space below or causing the outer container to scroll independently of the content.
The tab bar has a bottom border separating it from the content area, using the standard border-border color token.
The content area below the tab bar is independently scrollable (overflow-auto) so long result lists or stats panels don't push the tab bar off-screen.

groups.name: Tab Navigation (Search / Stats)
groups.description: Two tabs at the top of the page: Search (with search icon) and Stats (with bar chart icon). Clicking a tab switches the content area. The active tab has a card-colored background with a border (no bottom border to merge with content), while inactive tabs show muted text with hover highlight.

assertions.description: A 'Search' tab button is visible in the tab bar with a search icon.
A 'Stats' tab button is visible in the tab bar with a bar chart icon.

Clicking the Stats tab switches the content area to show the stats dashboard (KnowledgeStatsWidget + Provider Availability grid). Clicking the Search tab switches back to the search interface with mode buttons, input field, and results area. Only one tab's content is visible at a time.

The active tab has a card background (bg-card), foreground text color (text-foreground), and a border with no bottom border (border border-b-0). The inactive tab has muted text (text-muted-foreground) and no border or background.

groups.name: Search Mode Selector
groups.description: Three search mode buttons in the Search tab: 'Web Search' (globe icon), 'Error Research' (bug icon), 'Vuln Search' (shield icon). The active mode has primary-tinted background and border; inactive modes have muted text. Selecting a mode changes the input placeholder text and the API endpoint used for search.

assertions.description: A 'Web Search' mode button with a globe icon is visible and selectable.
An 'Error Research' mode button with a bug icon is visible and selectable.
A 'Vuln Search' mode button with a shield alert icon is visible and selectable.

Switching search modes changes the input placeholder text: Web shows 'Search the web for anything...', Error shows 'Paste an error message...', Vuln shows 'CVE ID or software name + version...'. This guides the user on what to enter for each mode.

The active search mode button has a primary-tinted background (bg-primary/10), primary text color, and a subtle primary border (border-primary/30). Inactive modes have muted text and no background. This provides clear visual feedback about which mode is selected.

groups.name: Search Input and Submit
groups.description: A text input field with a mode-specific icon (left) and a Search button (right). The input accepts text and supports Enter-to-submit. The Search button is disabled when the query is less than 2 characters or a search is in progress. During search, the button shows a spinning loader icon.

assertions.description: A text input field is visible with the current mode's placeholder text and a left-aligned icon matching the active search mode.
A 'Search' button with a search icon is visible to the right of the input field.
The Search button is disabled (opacity-50, cursor-not-allowed) when the input contains fewer than 2 characters. This prevents empty or single-character searches from hitting the API.
Pressing Enter in the search input submits the search (equivalent to clicking the Search button). Shift+Enter does NOT submit, allowing potential multi-line input in the future.
While a search is in progress, the Search button shows a spinning loader icon instead of the search icon, and the button is disabled. This provides visual feedback that the search is running.
assertions.precondition: A search has been submitted and is in progress

groups.name: Empty State and Error Handling
groups.description: Before any search, the results area shows an empty state with a file-search icon and helpful text. After a failed search, a red error banner appears. After a search with no results, a 'No results found' message is shown.

assertions.description: Before any search is performed, the results area shows a centered empty state with a FileSearch icon and the text 'Enter a search query to explore knowledge'.
assertions.precondition: No search has been performed yet

assertions.description: After a search that returns zero results, the text changes to 'No results found' instead of the initial prompt.
assertions.precondition: A search has been performed and returned zero results

assertions.description: When a search fails (API error, network failure), a red error banner appears at the top of the results area with an AlertCircle icon and the error message. The banner has a red-tinted background (bg-red-500/10) and border (border-red-500/20).
assertions.precondition: A search has failed with an error

groups.name: Search Result Cards
groups.description: Each search result is displayed as a card with: a provider-colored icon (left), title (bold, truncated), provider badge, relevance score percentage, optional CVSS badge, optional external link icon, and expandable content body. Results from different providers use different icon colors (DuckDuckGo=orange, Tavily=blue, Sploitus=red, Perplexity=purple, Local Cache=green).

assertions.description: Each result card shows: a colored provider icon, the result title as a bold heading, a provider name badge (text-[10px] bg-muted), and the content body below. Cards use bg-card with border-border styling.
Each result card displays the provider name as a small badge (e.g., 'DuckDuckGo', 'Tavily', 'Sploitus', 'Local Cache') below the title, helping users identify which source produced the result.
When a result has a relevance_score, it is displayed as a percentage (e.g., '95% relevant') in monospace font next to the provider badge.
assertions.precondition: A search has returned results with relevance scores

assertions.description: Vulnerability results with CVSS scores display a severity-colored badge: red for Critical (≥9.0), orange for High (≥7.0), yellow for Medium (≥4.0), green for Low (<4.0). The badge shows 'CVSS X.X' in semibold text.
assertions.precondition: A vulnerability search has returned results with CVSS scores

assertions.description: Results with a URL show an ExternalLink icon in the top-right corner that opens the source URL in a new tab (target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer). The icon has muted color that brightens on hover.
assertions.precondition: A result with a URL is displayed

assertions.description: Results with content longer than 500 characters show a 'Show more' link that expands to reveal the full content. When expanded, the link changes to 'Show less'. This prevents long results from dominating the results list.
assertions.precondition: A result with content > 500 characters is displayed

assertions.description: Above the result cards, a summary line shows the result count (e.g., '3 results') on the left and the providers used (e.g., 'via DuckDuckGo, Tavily') on the right.

Each provider uses a distinct icon color scheme: DuckDuckGo is orange (bg-orange-500/10 text-orange-400), Tavily is blue (bg-blue-500/10 text-blue-400), Sploitus/OSV are red (bg-red-500/10 text-red-400), Perplexity is purple (bg-purple-500/10 text-purple-400), Local Cache is green (bg-green-500/10 text-green-400). These colors help users quickly identify result sources.
assertions.precondition: Results from multiple providers are displayed

groups.name: Search Execution Behavior
groups.description: The search flow: user types query → selects mode → clicks Search or presses Enter → loading spinner appears → results populate or error shows. Each search mode calls a different backend endpoint: web→/knowledge/search-web, error→/knowledge/research-error, vulnerability→/knowledge/search-vulnerabilities. After a successful search, the stats are automatically invalidated to reflect the new query.

assertions.description: In Web Search mode, submitting a query calls POST /knowledge/search-web with {query, max_results: 5}. Results from DuckDuckGo (and optionally Tavily/Perplexity if they escalate) are displayed as cards. The provider_used field in the response populates the 'via ...' summary.
assertions.precondition: Web Search mode is active and a query with ≥2 chars is entered

assertions.description: In Error Research mode, submitting a query calls POST /knowledge/research-error with {error_message: query}. The backend builds a compound search query, checks local cache first (Tier 0), then escalates through web providers. Results are cached for future lookups via the knowledge flywheel.

In Vuln Search mode, submitting a query calls POST /knowledge/search-vulnerabilities with {query}. Results come from Sploitus and include CVSS scores, exploit availability, and CVE IDs. CVSS badges use severity-appropriate colors on the result cards.

groups.name: Knowledge Stats Widget
groups.description: The stats widget (visible on both the Stats tab as full-size and embeddable elsewhere as compact) displays: a header with Brain icon, 'Knowledge Acquisition' title, and uptime; a 2x2 grid of stat cells (Total Searches, Cache Hit Rate, Results Stored, Cache Hits); an Active Providers section with success/query badges; and a prompt injection warning when detections > 0. Data auto-refreshes every 30 seconds.

assertions.description: The stats widget header shows a Brain icon (text-orange-400), the text 'Knowledge Acquisition', and the formatted uptime (e.g., '5m', '2h 30m') on the right side.
The 'Total Searches' stat cell displays the cumulative number of searches performed since process start, formatted with locale-specific thousand separators.

The 'Cache Hit Rate' stat cell displays the percentage of searches served from local task_knowledge (Tier 0). Green color (text-green-400) when > 50%, yellow (text-yellow-400) otherwise. This is the key metric for knowledge flywheel effectiveness.
Cache Hit Rate is displayed in green when above 50% and yellow when at or below 50%, providing immediate visual feedback on flywheel health.

The 'Results Stored' stat cell shows the cumulative count of results ingested into task_knowledge. When dedup_skipped > 0, a subtitle shows 'N deduped' indicating how many duplicate results were skipped.

The 'Active Providers' section lists only providers that have handled at least one query. Each provider shows its short name and a success/total ratio (e.g., 'DDG 5/5'). Providers with failures use red-tinted styling (bg-red-500/10 text-red-400); healthy providers use muted styling.
assertions.precondition: At least one search has been performed

assertions.description: When prompt injection detections > 0, a yellow warning line appears at the bottom of the stats widget showing an AlertTriangle icon and the count (e.g., '2 prompt injections detected'). Pluralization is correct (1 = 'injection', 2+ = 'injections'). This warning is hidden when count is 0.
assertions.precondition: At least one prompt injection has been detected

assertions.description: While stats are loading, the widget shows a spinning Loader2 icon and the text 'Loading knowledge stats...' in muted color. The card maintains its bg-card border-border styling during loading.
assertions.precondition: Stats API has not yet responded

assertions.description: When the stats API is unavailable, the widget shows a Brain icon and 'Knowledge stats unavailable' in muted text. The card does not show an error banner — it degrades gracefully to a placeholder.

groups.name: Provider Availability Grid
groups.description: The Stats tab includes a Provider Availability card listing all 6 providers with their availability status (green dot = available, gray dot = unavailable) and API key requirement labels. This shows the user which search capabilities are active and what configuration is needed.

assertions.description: The Provider Availability card is visible on the Stats tab with a header reading 'Provider Availability' and rows for each provider.
All 6 providers are listed: DuckDuckGo, Tavily, UI Bridge, Sploitus, OSV.dev, Perplexity. Each shows its human-readable name on the left and availability status on the right.
assertions.precondition: Stats tab is active and providers have loaded

assertions.description: Available providers show a green dot (bg-green-400, w-2 h-2 rounded-full). Unavailable providers show a gray dot (bg-zinc-600). This binary indicator gives instant visual feedback.
Providers that require API keys (Tavily, Perplexity) show 'API key required' in muted text next to the availability dot. Free providers (DuckDuckGo, Sploitus, OSV.dev) do not show this label.

groups.name: Typography and Visual Design
groups.description: The Knowledge Explorer follows the runner's established design system: card components use bg-card with border-border, text uses the foreground/muted-foreground hierarchy, stat values use tabular-nums for aligned digits, provider badges use text-[10px], and section headers use uppercase tracking-wider. All text is legible against its background in both light and dark themes.

assertions.description: All cards (result cards, stats widget, provider grid) use the standard bg-card background with border-border border and rounded-lg corners. Headers use bg-muted/30 with a bottom border for visual separation.
Stat counter values use tabular-nums font variant so digits align vertically when numbers change (e.g., 9 to 10 doesn't shift adjacent elements). Values use text-sm font-semibold for prominence.

All text elements are legible against their backgrounds: primary text uses text-foreground on bg-card, secondary text uses text-muted-foreground, stat labels use text-[10px] text-muted-foreground, and colored stat values (green, yellow, blue, orange) have sufficient contrast against the card background in both light and dark themes.
The search input shows a focus ring (focus:ring-1 focus:ring-ring) when focused, providing clear keyboard navigation feedback. The input uses bg-muted background with border-border border.

groups.name: Data Consistency and Flywheel Verification
groups.description: The Knowledge Explorer can verify that the knowledge flywheel is working correctly by comparing stats before and after a search. A web search should increment total_searches, and if results are stored, results_ingested should increment. A subsequent identical search should show a cache hit if the flywheel stored the previous results.

assertions.description: After performing a web search, switching to the Stats tab should show total_searches incremented by 1 (stats auto-refresh every 30s). If results were found and stored, results_ingested should also increase. If the same query was searched before, cache_hits should increment instead.
assertions.precondition: A search has been performed and the Stats tab is viewed

assertions.description: Searching for the exact same query twice should show the second search results tagged with provider='local_knowledge' (if the flywheel stored the first results). The 'via Local Cache' text in the results summary confirms the flywheel is working. This verifies end-to-end: search → summarize → embed → store → retrieve.
assertions.precondition: The same query has been searched twice with the embedding service running

assertions.description: The providers listed in the Stats tab Provider Availability grid should match the providers shown in search result badges. If a provider shows available=false in the grid, no search results should ever show that provider's name in their badge.
